standard_prerequisites.name: Associated primes of a module over a Noetherian ring and the criterion that a map of finite modules is injective if it is injective after localising at every associated prime

standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the localisation criterion that turns the verification at associated primes into injectivity.

standard_prerequisites.name: Symmetric powers of a free module are free, and the multiplication by a linear form on them
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the maps whose injectivity is checked after localisation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Every ring is a filtered union of Noetherian subrings, and injectivity is preserved by such unions
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the general case to the Noetherian one.

core_obligations: Treat the case in which one of the a_i is a unit, where the statement reduces to the standard fact that a monic linear form is a nonzerodivisor (proof lines 7768-7771).

Assume R Noetherian, list its associated primes and for each associated prime q find an index i with a_i not in q, using that the annihilator of q is nonzero while x a_i is not zero for some i (proof lines 7772-7782).

Observe that a_i becomes a unit after localising at q, so the multiplication by the linear form on the free symmetric powers is injective there, and conclude injectivity of the map over R by the criterion at associated primes (proof lines 7782-7789).
Reduce the general case to the Noetherian one by writing R as the filtered union of Noetherian subrings containing the a_i and applying the previous step (proof lines 7791-7795).
proof_roadmap: Noetherian case: choose indices away from each associated prime (proof lines 7772-7782).
Localise and apply the associated prime criterion (proof lines 7782-7789).
General case by a filtered union of Noetherian subrings (proof lines 7791-7796).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that if the map sending x to the tuple (x a_1, ..., x a_n) is injective, then the linear form sum a_i t_i is a nonzerodivisor in the polynomial ring, and the proof is a 29-line argument in two cases. The case of a Noetherian ring works with the associated primes of the base: for each associated prime one of the a_i is not a unit and the symmetric powers involved are free, so localising at that prime makes the multiplication injective and the injectivity follows because a map that is injective at all associated primes is injective. The general case writes the ring as a filtered union of Noetherian subrings containing the a_i and applies the result to each of them. The localisation argument at associated primes is the substance, and the reduction to the Noetherian case is displayed.
